note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 3.11.5: 'RSVP must be able to force a (multicast) datagram to be sent on a specific outgoing real or virtual link, bypassing the normal routing mechanism.' Single-polarity capability. The lab routes the endpoint via link 1 in both namespaces; TestIntegrationRSVPPathCarriage fails unless PATH, PathTear and ResvConf to that endpoint leave on link 0 with link 0's peer MAC as L2 destination and arrive on peer0, while the Send control to link 1's peer is captured on link 1.
